title: Losing the Night
subtitle: Light pollution

segments.text: For all of human history, people looked up and saw the Milky Way. Today, about a third of humanity can't.
Street lights, buildings and billboards send light up into the sky, where it glows and hides the stars.
segments.headline: Light going up

segments.text: Studies using citizen scientists suggest the night sky is getting brighter by about ten percent a year.
And there's a new problem. More than ten thousand satellites now orbit Earth. Most of them belong to Starlink.
They reflect sunlight and leave streaks across telescope images, and their radio signals can disturb radio telescopes.
segments.headline: Streaks across the sky

segments.text: Darkness matters for nature too. Baby sea turtles, birds and insects get confused by artificial light.
segments.headline: Animals need the dark

segments.text: The good news: light pollution is easy to fix. Point lights downward, use warmer colors, and turn off what you don't need.
segments.headline: Easy to fix

segments.text: Dark sky parks around the world protect the night. Visit one, and you'll never forget it.
segments.headline: Visit a dark sky park
